column1: # div-sites.tsv — the reviewed set of `\div` sites in the authored corpus.
# Read harness/test-div-contract.sh before you edit this file. It is the gate
# that holds the tree to this inventory, and its header carries the bug.
# THE SHORT VERSION. TLC 2026.07.31.184830 breaks the contract its own bundled
# Naturals.tla states. `-17 \div 5` comes back -3, so `5 * -3 + 3` is -12 and
# not -17. The quotient truncates toward zero where the contract forces it to
# round down. A corpus that takes its answers from TLC's exit codes will
# therefore bake TLC's bug as the answer, and an item over a negative dividend
# "The dividend can never be negative" is not something a scan can decide, so
# this file does not try. It records the sites somebody has read, and the gate
# fails on a site that is not here and on an entry whose site has gone. That
# is enough to make a new `\div` stop an author and ask about its dividend.
# WHEN THE GATE GOES RED, GO AND READ THE DIVIDEND. Never add a row here to
# quiet the gate. The row is worth nothing unless somebody looked first.
#   2  path      repo-relative, as `git ls-files` prints it
#   3  count     how many times that window occurs in that file, exact
#   4  window    the `\div` token plus one whitespace-separated token each side
#   5  reason    why the dividend is safe, or why the site is prose
# THE KEY IS THE WINDOW AND NOT THE LINE, which is the one design choice worth
# knowing about. A line number goes stale on the next edit above it, and a
# whole line carries the prose around the operator, so rewording an item's
# explanation would redden a gate that has nothing to say about prose. The
# window holds the operands and drops the sentence. `17 \div 5` is the same
# site whether it moves down the file or the line around it is rewritten.
# The price is the count column. Four items state `17 \div 5`, so they share
# one row, and a fifth reddens the gate until somebody reads it and bumps the
# count to 5. That is the friction working rather than failing.
# A RENAMED FILE READS AS A VANISHED SITE, on purpose. The old path stops
# resolving and the gate says so, which is louder than a key that follows the
# file around and quietly stops asserting anything.
# PROSE SITES ARE IN, and some of their dividends are negative. The comment
# block in swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv and the section in swipe/README.md both
# document this bug and both quote `-17 \div 5`. They are here with that as
# their reason. A gate that stripped comments would be a gate over executed
# code, and a wrong quotient stated in an ANSWER.md is read by a learner just
# `%` IS NOT IN THIS FILE, and that is a decision rather than an oversight.
# The remainder half of the contract holds: `-17 % 5` is 3, inside `0..4` as
# Naturals.tla requires, and swipe item L0-T5-44 depends on `-5 % 3` being 1.
# So a `%` site carries no wrong answer, while the character itself cannot be
# told from a percentage or a printf format without a TLA+ parser. 506 tracked
# lines under these roots carry a `%` against 83 `\div` occurrences, so an
# inventory over it would be mostly noise and would rot into a waiver.
# WHAT WAS SEARCHED, per the CLAUDE.md rule that a claim of completeness names
# its search. Every tracked file under drill/ reading/ recall/ completion/
# exercises/ chapter/ swipe/ and harness/fixtures/, selected through
# `git ls-files` and matched with GNU grep from a script. chapter/ carries no
# site today and is in the roots so that the first one is caught.
# 76 rows, 83 occurrences over 70 lines, 2222 tracked files, measured
# 2026-10-18. Three of those rows are the last three in the file, and the gate
# found them rather than the author: they landed on main while this bead was
# in flight, and the first run after the rebase named all three.
